paragraphs: Here's what hits me, friend. Moses hears he won't enter the land, and he doesn't argue or sulk. He turns around and prays for the people. His ask is about the flock, not about himself: he doesn't want the congregation of the LORD to be "like sheep without a shepherd" (Numbers 27:17).

Now look at how God answers. He doesn't leave a gap. He names Joshua son of Nun, "a man with the Spirit in him" (Numbers 27:18), and has Moses commission him in front of the whole congregation (Numbers 27:19). Moses does it just as the LORD said (Numbers 27:22-23). A hard word about Moses (Numbers 27:13-14) sits right beside a God who still looks after His people.

So what does that mean for you, baker? The work you hold is bigger than your part in it. Hold it with open hands, and pray for the people who come after you, the way Moses prayed for Israel. I held my stamper like I'd be on that counter forever, and look where it got me: the back of a drawer. God still cared for His people then, and He still does.
